title: Council orientation sessions on township and county services
subtitle: Integrity Commissioner role, municipal finance, fire training, social services, solid waste, planning under Bill 23, and emergency management
overview: The December 8, 2022 Committee of the Whole meeting was an orientation day for the incoming Council. No motions were recorded in the minutes, so no decisions or recommendations were made. The day was a series of presentations by outside advisors, township staff and County of Wellington staff.

Morning sessions covered Council's responsibilities under the Code of Conduct and the Conflict of Interest Act, including the role of the Integrity Commissioner. A Ministry of Municipal Affairs advisor then explained municipal government, changes to Council composition, Council's role as lawmakers, and the fiscal context.

In the afternoon, township and county staff covered asset management, development charges and property tax policy. County staff then outlined the fire training program, social services (children's early years, housing and Ontario Works) and solid waste services. The final session covered county planning, including emerging issues related to Bill 23, climate change initiatives, GIS mapping tools, source water protection and emergency management.
For residents, the meeting shows the background information Council received before taking up the decisions ahead of it.
